title: Knowing Is Not Committing: Replicating MIT's weight-space edit and programming a truth-gated reflex into a 0.8B reasoning model (report)
read_level: partial (Zenodo record/API returned HTTP 403; read the v0.5 report markdown from the GitHub release the Zenodo record links as supplement, github.com/NeoCortex0815/knowing-is-not-committing tag v0.5, report/Knowing_Is_Not_Committing_v0.5.md: header, abstract, TL;DR, Erratum, Secs 1, 2, 3.1-3.3, part of 3.6, 5-8 read; Secs 3.4-3.5, 3.7-3.14 body, 4 and Appendix A not read; v0.2 PDF not read). why_wsp: Rebuilds MIT's Qwen3.5-0.8B loop-reversal edit and hand-constructs weight edits (own loop direction, ERGORE closing coupling, a 16-neuron truth-gated reflex 'WT' in layer 15) from measured directions and gradients of activations; edits are author-directed, with Claude Opus 5.5 implementing code, not an autonomous LLM editor loop.
domain: LLM math reasoning (reasoning loops and answer commitment, MATH-500, MATH train, IFEval)
editor: Author-directed; 'Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) served as coding and analysis assistant: it implemented the code, ran the experiments' (Sec 8). Directions derived by mean differences/probes, not by an agent search.
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B (hybrid GatedDeltaNet / full attention, 24 layers), q8_0 GGUF via llama.cpp
interface: closed form (hand-constructed rank-1 terms and rewritten neurons from measured directions/gradients)
loop: n/a (author-run development and pre-registered tests; no autonomous editor loop)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: WT reflex: "16 rarely active neurons in layer 15 are rewritten" (Sec 3.6); MIT edit described as "about 0.016 % of the weights" (Sec 1); own direction recipe: "layers 15 and 19, top-64 columns, α = 6" (Sec 3.2)

headline_results.claim: Sampling protocol effect on MIT's edit
headline_results.quote: MIT's published edit scores 55 % with vLLM-style sampling and 25 % with llama.cpp's default sampling
Our own direction (cosine 0.76/0.77 to MIT's) lifts the base model from 10 % to 37.5 % on those 40 problems

headline_results.claim: ERGORE vs MIT on fresh problems

headline_results.quote: WT-A closes right after the correct value in 65 % of opportunities, MIT in 36 % (p = 0.0001)
Accuracy there: 63 vs 82 of 140 (−13.6 points, paired bootstrap 95 % CI −21.4 to −6.4)
on fresh problems the model reopens its reasoning after 77 % of its closes

headline_results.claim: Answer mode vs MIT with thinking
headline_results.quote: 76 vs 82 of 140 for MIT with thinking (−4.3 points, 95 % CI −13.6 to +4.3)
It solves 77 of 150, against 69 for answer mode alone (H1 "holds") and 67 for MIT with thinking (H2 "beats MIT": +10, one-sided McNemar p = 0.026, unadjusted)
IFEval 61/120, against 74 without the push (p = 0.041) and 87 for MIT

headline_results.claim: v0.5: external SGNE-CC under their protocol
headline_results.quote: 22 of 50 against 5, committing to 80 % of the correct values it finds

cost.claim: Tokens per correct answer (inference, not editing cost)
cost.quote: It needs 15,500 instead of 36,800 tokens per correct answer.
one laptop GPU (8 GB) via llama.cpp (q8_0 GGUF)

baselines_and_controls: MIT's published edit (rebuilt from logs) with thinking and in answer mode; unedited base; own-direction edit without trigger; ERGORE; sampling-setting comparison; second seeds on parts; IFEval harm check; external SGNE-CC edit and ablations built from its released tensors; Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base.
runs_and_variance: Mostly single seed; second seeds for Set B and parts of 161-300. Quote: 'Most results rest on a single seed; second seeds exist for parts of the data.' Also: 'MIT itself varies by 6 of 40 between seeds on one block.' (Sec 5)
robustness_of_edits: Transfer to fresh problems tested (ERGORE's tie on 1-160 did not transfer; WT-A's dev-set lead reversed); IFEval side-effect check; sampling-protocol sensitivity (llama.cpp vs vLLM-style) reported; quantized q8_0 runs vs bf16 teacher-forcing noted as a limitation
verification: Statistical with dated pre-registration log (threshold readings, exact McNemar, Holm over ~40 readings for main effects); v0.4 erratum corrected a silent grading fallback (65 correct answers counted wrong).
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a (no LLM editor). Linear truth probe evidence that the target model 'knows' correct values before committing (AUC 0.96 practice; N31 AUC 0.51 for model's own closing tendency vs 0.68 probe).
limitations_stated: One 0.8B model; mostly one seed; development sets reused; post hoc mechanism results on small cells; teacher-forcing audit in bf16 vs llama.cpp q8_0 runs; narrow proxies (IFEval, MATH); N30 uses MATH train problems; B+H rule chosen after viewing 161-260; v0.5 sections on 50 problems with readings fixed only in dated log.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (MIT CSAIL, 2026-11-02) and released logs
SGNE-CC by Igor M. Zhuk (Hugging Face)
Zhang et al. 2025; Orgad et al. 2025; Arditi et al. 2024; Li et al. 2026
notes_for_survey: Independent replication and dissection of the MIT Qwen3.5-0.8B edit on consumer hardware, with pre-registration and a published erratum. Reports that sampling settings alone move MIT's edit from 25% to 55% on 40 problems, and that hand-written edits matching MIT on development problems did not transfer to fresh ones. Versioned record: corpus date is v0.2, current is v0.5.
